producer.def: An organism that makes its own food from light (or chemicals) and simple substances, such as a plant, alga or photosynthetic bacterium; also called an autotroph.

primary-productivity.def: The rate at which producers capture energy and build organic matter by photosynthesis in an area, such as kcal per square meter per year.

gpp.def: Gross primary productivity: the total rate at which producers capture energy by photosynthesis, before any is used for their own respiration.

npp.def: Net primary productivity: GPP minus the energy producers use for their own respiration (NPP = GPP - R). It is the energy stored as new plant matter and available to the animals that eat plants.
